1.note: Here, the word **saying** introduces a direct quotation. See how you translated **saying** in [1:1](ta:01).

2.note: The term **Speak to Aaron and say to him** introduces a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language. It may not be necessary to represent this term explicitly. Alternate translation: [Say to Aaron]

The text includes quotations within quotations. If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [and say to him that when he lifts up]

The implication is that Aaron would lift up the lamps to put them in their proper places on the lampstand. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [When you lift up the lamps and put them on the lampstand]

The implication is that the lampstand should be set up in such a way that the seven lamps illuminate the area in front of it. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the seven lamps must be oriented so that they shine]

Here, **to the face of** represents being in front of the lampstand. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [on the place before the lampstand]

3.note: The implication is that the lamps were positioned so they would shine forward from the lampstand. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [To shine to the front of the face of the lampstand he lifted up its lamps]
See how you translated this phrase in 8:2. Alternate translation: [Facing the place before the lampstand]

The implication is that someone needed to put the lamps in their places on the lampstand to get them ready to burn. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. See how you translated the similar phrase in 8:2. Alternate translation: [he lifted up the lamps and put them on the lampstand]

4.note: The author is using the possessive form to describe a **lampstand** that was made by a specific kind of **work**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [how the lampstand was made]

A **hammered work** is a kind of metal object that is formed by repeatedly striking a sheet of metal to shape it. If your readers would not be familiar with what a hammered work is, you could use a more general term or explain it in a footnote. Alternate translation: [constructed from a sheet of gold that was hammered into shape, it was constructed this way]

The author is referring to all of the lampstand by naming two major components, **its side** and **its blossom**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in its entirety] or [completely, including its side and its blossom]

A **blossom** is a kind of flower that decorated the golden lampstand. If your readers would not be familiar with what a blossom is, you could use a more general term or explain it in a footnote. See the description of the lampstand in Exodus 25:33–36. Alternate translation: [the blossom that decorated it]

In this verse, the word **blossom** is singular in form, but it refers to all the flower decorations on the lampstand as a group. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural form of “blossom.” Alternate translation: [its blossoms]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **appearance**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [According to what Yahweh showed Moses about how the lampstand should look]

The implication is that someone made the lampstand at Moses’s direction rather than Moses making it himself. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [so he had the workers make the lampstand]

6.note: Here, Moses is speaking as if the Levites were an object that could be physically **taken** from among the Israelites. He means that they should be selected and set apart from the rest of the people. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Select the Levites from among the sons of Israel]

7.note: The implication is that some of these instructions will be carried out by Moses and others will be carried out by the Levites themselves. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And here is how]

Sprinkling the water of the sin offering was a symbolic action by which the priests showed that the Levites were being purified and made clean for their service. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [Sprinkle on them the water of the sin offering to purify them]

Here, **sin offering** represents the purification from sin that occurs when a **sin offering** is offered. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [purification]

The phrase **pass a razor over all their flesh** is a common expression of his culture to mean “cut off the hair from their entire body.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And they shall use a razor to cut off the hair on their entire body]

A **razor** is a kind of cutting tool used for shaving hair. If your readers would not be familiar with what a razor is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. See how you translated **razor** in 6:5. Alternate translation: [a shaving tool]

Here, the word **and** introduces a summary or conclusion for this section. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this more explicit. Alternate translation: [and thus they shall cleanse themselves]

8.note: Here, Yahweh uses the phrase **son of cattle** to indicate that the bull was young. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated this phrase in 7:15. Alternate translation: [a young one … a young one]

The expression **mixed with the oil** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. See how you translated this phrase in 6:15. Alternate translation: [flour that they had mixed with the oil]

Yahweh is not referring to a specific **oil**. He means oil in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. See how you translated this phrase in 6:15. Alternate translation: [with oil]

Here, Yahweh could be telling Moses that: (1) he must be the one who offers the second bull. Alternate translation: [And you yourself shall take] (2) he must instruct the Levites to offer the second bull. Alternate translation: [And you shall have them take]

If your language would not represent a number in a form such as **a second bull**, you could represent this number in a form that your language would use. Alternate translation: [another bull] or [bull two]

9.note: Here, **to the face of** represents being in front of the tent of meeting. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [before the tent of meeting]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **congregation** that is made up of **the sons of Israel**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the congregation that consists of all the sons of Israel]

10.note: Here, **to the face of** represents being in front of Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [before Yahweh]
Yahweh is speaking of himself in the third person as **Yahweh**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [to my face]

To lay hands on the Levites was a symbolic action by which the Israelites could have shown: (1) that the Levites were substitutes for them. Alternate translation: [and the sons of Israel shall lay their hands on the Levites to designate the Levites as their substitutes] (2) that the Levites were being dedicated to God. Alternate translation: [and the sons of Israel shall lay their hands on the Levites to dedicate them to God]

By **the sons of Israel**, Yahweh means the leaders of Israel who were representing all of Israel in this ceremony. It would not be possible for all the Israelites to lay their hands on the Levites. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and the leaders of the sons of Israel]

11.q: וְ⁠הֵנִיף֩ אַהֲרֹ֨ן אֶת־הַ⁠לְוִיִּ֤ם תְּנוּפָה֙ לִ⁠פְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה
11.note: Here, Moses is speaking of presenting the Levites to Yahweh as if they were a **raised offering**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And Aaron shall dedicate the Levites to Yahweh as he does when he raises a raised offering]

Yahweh is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [And Aaron shall offer the Levites as a raised offering]

The expression **raised offering** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is a priest. Alternate translation: [as an offering that the priests raise]

Yahweh is speaking of himself in the third person as **Yahweh**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [to my face … my service]
Here, **to the face of** represents being in front of Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [before Yahweh]

Here, just as in Numbers 4, the words **serve** and **service** refer to tasks of setting up, taking down, and carrying the sacred tent. See how you translated these words in 4:30. Alternate translation: [for the physical labor required to move]

Yahweh is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [to serve]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **service** that is done for **Yahweh**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the service they do for Yahweh]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **service**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [as Yahweh needs to be served]

12.q: וְ⁠הַ⁠לְוִיִּם֙ יִסְמְכ֣וּ אֶת־יְדֵי⁠הֶ֔ם עַ֖ל רֹ֣אשׁ הַ⁠פָּרִ֑ים
12.note: To lay hands on the bulls was a symbolic action by which the Levites could have shown: (1) that the bulls were substitutes for the Levites. Alternate translation: [And the Levites shall lay their hands on the head of the bulls to designate the bulls as their substitutes] (2) that the bulls were being dedicated to God. Alternate translation: [And the Levites shall lay their hands on the head of the bulls to dedicate them to God]

This is a command addressed to Moses. Yahweh could be indicating that: (1) Moses should have the priest make the offerings. Alternate translation: [and have a priest make] (2) Moses should make the offerings himself. Alternate translation: [and you must make]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **atonement**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [to redeem the Levites and restore them to Yahweh]

13.note: Here, **to the face of** represents being in front of Aaron and his sons. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [before Aaron and before his sons]

Here, Yahweh is speaking of dedicating the Levites to Yahweh as if their dedication were a **raised offering** that was lifted up to him. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated the similar phrase in 8:11. Alternate translation: [and you shall dedicate the Levites to Yahweh as you do when you raise a raised offering]

Yahweh is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [and you shall offer them as a raised offering to Yahweh]

The expression **raised offering** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is a priest. Alternate translation: [as an offering that the priests raise]
Yahweh is speaking of himself in the third person as **Yahweh**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [to me]

14.note: Here, the word **And** introduces a summary or conclusion for this section. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this more explicit. Alternate translation: [And thus you shall separate the Levites]

15.q: וְ⁠אַֽחֲרֵי־כֵן֙ יָבֹ֣אוּ הַ⁠לְוִיִּ֔ם לַ⁠עֲבֹ֖ד אֶת־אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֑ד וְ⁠טִֽהַרְתָּ֣ אֹתָ֔⁠ם וְ⁠הֵנַפְתָּ֥ אֹתָ֖⁠ם תְּנוּפָֽה
15.note: The event in the second clauses (**you shall cleanse them and you shall raise them as a raised offering**) will happen before the events in the first clause (**the Levites shall go to serve the tent of meeting**). If having the clauses in this order would make the sequence unclear, you can change the order. Alternate translation: [And you shall cleanse the Levites and you shall raise them as a raised offering, and after that the Levites shall go to serve the tent of meeting]

Yahweh is using **shall go to serve** as a common expression of his culture to mean “shall be capable of serving.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [shall be capable of serving]
See how you translated this clause in 8:13.

16.q: נְתֻנִ֨ים נְתֻנִ֥ים הֵ֨מָּה֙ לִ֔⁠י מִ⁠תּ֖וֹךְ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל
16.note: Here, Yahweh is speaking as if the Israelites were actually **given** to Yahweh like objects that could be handed over. This represents the formal dedication and appointment of people for service to Yahweh. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [they are appointed, appointed to me out of all the sons of Israel]

The expression **are given, given** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is God. Alternate translation: [I have given them, given them to myself]

Yahweh is repeating forms of the verb **given** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [they are wholly given]

It might seem that the expression **the opener of every womb, the firstborn of** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you could shorten it. Alternate translation: [the firstborn of]

Yahweh is using **the opener of every womb** as a common expression of his culture to mean “the first child of every woman.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated this phrase in 3:12. Alternate translation: [the first child of every woman]

Here and throughout this chapter, the implication is that **firstborn** refers specifically to firstborn males. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the firstborn males of]

By **taken them for me**, God means he has selected them to serve him at the tent of meeting. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [I have selected them to serve me at the tent of meeting]

17.note: Here, **man** and **animal** represent people and animals in general, not specific people or animals. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use expressions that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [among the men and among the animals]

Here the masculine term **man** has a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [among the human]

The expression **On the day of** is a common expression of his culture to mean “at the time when.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [At the time when I struck down]

By **my striking down**, God means when he killed all the firstborn sons of the Egyptians. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. See the discussion of the term “struck” in the Introduction to Numbers. Alternate translation: [my slaying]

18.note: By **I have taken the Levites**, God means he selected and set apart the Levites for special service to him. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And I have selected the Levites to serve me at the tent of meeting]

19.note: Here, Yahweh is speaking as if the Levites were actually **given ones** who were presented as gifts to Aaron and his sons. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And I appointed the Levites as appointed ones]

Yahweh is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [And I gave the Levites]

Yahweh is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [to serve]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **service** that is done **for the sons of Israel**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the service they do for the sake of the sons of Israel]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **service**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [for the sake of serving the sons of Israel]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **atonement**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [to redeem the sons of Israel]

The word translated as **And** here indicates that what follows is a result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a result of what came before. Alternate translation: [As a result, a plague will not be]

The term **plague** refers to any kind of severe disaster or terrible trouble. If your readers would not be familiar with what a plague is, you could use a more general term or explain it in a footnote. Alternate translation: [a disaster] or [terrible trouble]

20.q: וַ⁠יַּ֨עַשׂ מֹשֶׁ֧ה וְ⁠אַהֲרֹ֛ן וְ⁠כָל־עֲדַ֥ת בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לַ⁠לְוִיִּ֑ם כְּ֠⁠כֹל אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֨ה יְהוָ֤ה אֶת־מֹשֶׁה֙ לַ⁠לְוִיִּ֔ם כֵּן־עָשׂ֥וּ לָ⁠הֶ֖ם בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל
20.note: It might seem that the expression **thus the sons of Israel did to them** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you could shorten it. Alternate translation: [And Moses, and Aaron and all the congregation of the sons of Israel, did to the Levites exactly according to all that Yahweh had commanded Moses for the Levites]

The author is using the possessive form to describe a **congregation** that is made up of **the sons of Israel**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. See how you translated this phrase in 8:9. Alternate translation: [the congregation that consists of all the sons of Israel]

21.q: וַ⁠יָּ֨נֶף אַהֲרֹ֥ן אֹתָ֛⁠ם תְּנוּפָ֖ה לִ⁠פְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה
21.note: See how you translated the similar phrase in 8:11.

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **atonement**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [And Aaron offered sacrifices to redeem the Levites and restore them to Yahweh]

22.note: The phrase **went to serve** is a common expression of his culture to mean “were capable of serving” or “began their service.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated the similar phrase in 8:15. Alternate translation: [were capable of serving]

Yahweh is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [to serve]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **service**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [as they must serve]

Here, **to the face of** represents being in front of Aaron and his sons. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. See how you translated these words in 8:13. Alternate translation: [before Aaron and before his sons]
The pronoun **they** refers to the Levites. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the people of Israel]

24.note: Yahweh is using **This is what is for the Levites** as a common expression of his culture to mean “Here is what the Levites should do.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Here is what the Levites should do]

24.q: מִ⁠בֶּן֩ חָמֵ֨שׁ וְ⁠עֶשְׂרִ֤ים שָׁנָה֙ וָ⁠מַ֔עְלָ⁠ה יָבוֹא֙
24.note: Yahweh is not referring to a specific Levite. He means Levites who meet this requirement in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [From sons of 25 years and upward they shall come]

24.q: מִ⁠בֶּן֩ חָמֵ֨שׁ וְ⁠עֶשְׂרִ֤ים שָׁנָה֙ וָ⁠מַ֔עְלָ⁠ה יָבוֹא֙
24.note: The phrase **from a son of 25 years** is a common expression of this culture that means “from age 25” or “starting at 25 years old.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated the similar phrase in 1:3. Alternate translation: [Those who are 25 years old or older shall come] or [Those aged 25 and above shall come]

Yahweh is using **come to fight** as a common expression of this culture to mean “begin doing military service.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated this phrase in 4:23. Alternate translation: [he can fight]

Here, Yahweh is speaking of serving in the tabernacle as if it were **fighting in the army**. This metaphor implies dedication and discipline in service. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated this phrase in 4:23. Alternate translation: [to be part of the group of workers]

Yahweh is using a construction in which a verb (**fight**) and its object (**army**) come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [to be in the army]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **service**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [to serve at]

25.q: וּ⁠מִ⁠בֶּן֙ חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה יָשׁ֖וּב מִ⁠צְּבָ֣א הָ⁠עֲבֹדָ֑ה וְ⁠לֹ֥א יַעֲבֹ֖ד עֽוֹד
25.note: Yahweh is not referring to a specific Levite. He means Levites who meet this qualification in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. See how you chose to translate 8:24. Alternate translation: [And from sons of 50 years old they shall return from the army of service, and they shall not serve more]

The phrase **a son of 50 years** is a common expression of this culture that means that a person has the characteristic of being at least 50 years old. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an equivalent expression from your language or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Those who are 50 years old or older shall return] or [Those aged 50 and above shall return]

Yahweh is using **he shall return from the army** as a common expression of this culture to mean “he cannot be in the army.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated the opposite figure of speech in 8:24. Alternate translation: [he cannot be in the army]
If your language does not use abstract nouns for the idea of **service**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [from the army that serves]

Here, Yahweh is speaking of the group of workers as if it were an **army**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated the similar figure of speech in 8:24. Alternate translation: [from being part of the group of workers for]

26.q: וְ⁠שֵׁרֵ֨ת אֶת־אֶחָ֜י⁠ו בְּ⁠אֹ֤הֶל מוֹעֵד֙ לִ⁠שְׁמֹ֣ר מִשְׁמֶ֔רֶת וַ⁠עֲבֹדָ֖ה לֹ֣א יַעֲבֹ֑ד
26.note: Yahweh is not referring to one specific Levite. He means Levites over 50 years old in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use expressions that would be more natural in your language. See how you chose to translate 8:24–25. Alternate translation: [And they shall minister to their brothers in the tent of meeting to keep keeping, but they shall not serve service]

Here, Yahweh is using the term **brothers** to describe fellow members of the tribe of Levi. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to the other Levites]

By **keep keeping** and **serve service**, Yahweh means to guard the holy things and do the physical work associated with moving them. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. See the chapter introduction for more information. Alternate translation: [to guard the holy things, but he shall not do the physical labor required to move them]

Yahweh is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [to keep, but he shall not serve]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **service**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [in any way that the Levites serve]

By **their keepings**, Yahweh means the duties and responsibilities that God has assigned to the Levites. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [That is what you must command the Levites concerning their keepings]

The implication is that the Levites had specific duties guarding the sanctuary and assisting with its maintenance. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. See the chapter introduction for more information. Alternate translation: [in their guard duties]
